tactical_cards.name: Remove a fixed model assumption
tactical_cards.tactical_move: Replace a required model, calibration or distributional assumption with a weaker observable condition.
tactical_cards.when_to_apply: Use when the robot must operate under unknown contact, friction, terrain or dynamics.
success_conditions: The weaker condition occurs in the target operating envelope.
A tightness or failure-case analysis shows the removed assumption was binding.
failure_modes: An equally strong hidden model is reintroduced.
tactical_cards.trigger: A controller or estimator fails when a nominal model, calibration, friction or distribution assumption drifts.
tactical_cards.changed_object: The required model assumption is replaced by an observable condition or bounded uncertainty set.
tactical_cards.retained_invariant: Task, sensing interface, actuation limits and evaluation denominator remain fixed.
five_step_recipe: Name the inherited assumption and the failure it causes.
Define the weaker observable condition and its operating range.
Implement the mechanism without reintroducing the original assumption.
Compare against the nominal model and an oracle-model upper bound.
Sweep the violated assumption until both methods reach their failure boundary.
tactical_cards.differentiation_within_parent: Unlike locus relocation, this changes assumption strength rather than where a signal is enforced.
robotics_failure_modes: Online identification recreates an equally strong hidden model.
The observable condition cannot be measured at control rate.
Safety depends on an untested uncertainty bound.
tactical_cards.decisive_experiment: Sweep model mismatch over a predeclared range and test whether the new mechanism retains the claimed outcome after the nominal method crosses its boundary.
tactical_cards.semantic_negative_control: Give the baseline the same compute and observations but a shuffled or stale condition estimate.
tactical_cards.prior_art_search_signature: robotics unknown dynamics OR friction robust control weaker assumption observable condition model-free boundary
step_by_step_recipe: Name the inherited assumption and the failure it causes.
Define the weaker observable condition and its operating range.
Implement the mechanism without reintroducing the original assumption.
Compare against the nominal model and an oracle-model upper bound.
Sweep the violated assumption until both methods reach their failure boundary.

tactical_cards.name: Limit characterization and strict surpass
tactical_cards.tactical_move: Establish a stability, safety, bandwidth, sample or planning boundary, then exceed it with a named mechanism.
tactical_cards.when_to_apply: Use when a matched baseline has a sharp and reproducible boundary.
success_conditions: The boundary is measured under the same regime.
The improvement exceeds uncertainty and has a mechanism.
failure_modes: Only an empirical improvement is shown with no boundary or tightness.
tactical_cards.trigger: A matched baseline has a sharp reproducible stability, safety, bandwidth, sample or planning boundary.
tactical_cards.changed_object: The mechanism that moves one named limit.
tactical_cards.retained_invariant: Robot, task, information, compute, safety protocol and uncertainty accounting remain matched.
five_step_recipe: Define and reproduce the inherited limit.
Measure uncertainty around the boundary.
Name the mechanism predicted to move it.
Run matched sweeps through both boundaries.
Remove the mechanism and test return to the old limit.
tactical_cards.differentiation_within_parent: This requires an explicit inherited limit and strict surpass, not a generic average improvement.
robotics_failure_modes: The old boundary is under-tuned.
Regimes differ across sweeps.
Uncertainty overlaps the claimed surpass.
tactical_cards.decisive_experiment: Sweep the limiting variable under an identical regime and show a non-overlapping boundary shift that vanishes when the named mechanism is removed.
tactical_cards.semantic_negative_control: Add a cost-matched mechanism that cannot affect the named limit.
tactical_cards.prior_art_search_signature: robot stability safety bandwidth sample planning limit boundary strict surpass matched sweep
step_by_step_recipe: Define and reproduce the inherited limit.
Measure uncertainty around the boundary.
Name the mechanism predicted to move it.
Run matched sweeps through both boundaries.
Remove the mechanism and test return to the old limit.

tactical_cards.name: Controlled diagnostic construction
tactical_cards.tactical_move: Build a one-variable-isolated intervention or measurement instrument.
tactical_cards.when_to_apply: Use when a robot claim can be explained by hardware, data, tuning or human adaptation confounds.
success_conditions: The intervention has a downstream prediction.
Controls are matched in cost and information.
failure_modes: Only the intermediate metric changes, not the task outcome.
tactical_cards.trigger: A claimed mechanism can still be explained by hardware, data, compute, tuning or operator adaptation.
tactical_cards.changed_object: One load-bearing variable is intervened on while the visible interface and resource budget stay fixed.
tactical_cards.retained_invariant: Hardware, data split, observations, tuning budget, task and denominator remain matched.
five_step_recipe: List the mechanism and strongest alternative explanation.
Choose one intervention that separates their predictions.
Construct a cost- and information-matched semantic control.
Freeze the downstream metric and decision rule.
Run the intervention and require a predicted task-level divergence.
tactical_cards.differentiation_within_parent: This constructs a new causal diagnostic; it is not a generic ablation that merely deletes a module.
robotics_failure_modes: Intervention changes controller stability or latency.
Negative control is cheaper or less informed.
Only an internal proxy changes.
Operator behavior adapts across conditions.
tactical_cards.decisive_experiment: Intervene on the load-bearing variable and its semantic control under matched cost; the two must produce different predeclared downstream signatures.
tactical_cards.semantic_negative_control: Preserve dimensions, compute and surface statistics while permuting or misbinding the claimed semantics.
tactical_cards.prior_art_search_signature: robotics mechanism diagnostic causal intervention semantic negative control matched ablation confound
step_by_step_recipe: List the mechanism and strongest alternative explanation.
Choose one intervention that separates their predictions.
Construct a cost- and information-matched semantic control.
Freeze the downstream metric and decision rule.
Run the intervention and require a predicted task-level divergence.

tactical_cards.name: Self-supervised signal engineering
tactical_cards.tactical_move: Derive supervision from temporal, geometric, cross-view or task consistency.
tactical_cards.when_to_apply: Use when robot labels are expensive but structure is observable.
success_conditions: The pretext signal is tied to the downstream property.
Signal removal degrades the intended behavior.
failure_modes: The pretext is generic and unrelated to the task.
tactical_cards.trigger: Labels are scarce while a temporal, geometric, cross-view or task consistency relation is observable.
tactical_cards.changed_object: The source and semantics of the supervisory signal.
tactical_cards.retained_invariant: Model capacity, data frames, optimizer budget and downstream evaluation remain matched.
five_step_recipe: Name the downstream property that lacks labels.
Identify an observable consistency relation.
Construct the signal without target leakage.
Train matched supervised and generic-pretext controls.
Remove or misbind the signal and test the downstream property.
tactical_cards.differentiation_within_parent: This engineers supervision from robot structure; it does not merely add an auxiliary generic loss.
robotics_failure_modes: Future or privileged state leaks into the signal.
Pretext success is disconnected from task behavior.
More frames or compute explain the gain.
tactical_cards.decisive_experiment: Preserve data and compute while removing the structural correspondence; only the mechanism-aligned signal should retain the downstream gain.
tactical_cards.semantic_negative_control: Permute temporal, geometric or cross-view correspondence while preserving marginal statistics.
tactical_cards.prior_art_search_signature: robot self-supervised temporal geometric cross-view task consistency downstream property
step_by_step_recipe: Name the downstream property that lacks labels.
Identify an observable consistency relation.
Construct the signal without target leakage.
Train matched supervised and generic-pretext controls.
Remove or misbind the signal and test the downstream property.

tactical_cards.name: Residual mechanism liberation
tactical_cards.tactical_move: Expose the physical or modeling residual that a fixed generator cannot explain.
tactical_cards.when_to_apply: Use when sim-to-real, friction, contact or dynamics residuals dominate the error.
success_conditions: The residual is measurable and closed by the mechanism.
A residual-removal control returns performance toward baseline.
failure_modes: The residual model becomes a generic error-corrector with no mechanism.
tactical_cards.trigger: A reproducible physical or modeling residual dominates error after the fixed generator is matched.
tactical_cards.changed_object: The explicit residual channel and mechanism that closes it.
tactical_cards.retained_invariant: Generator, observations, training budget, task and evaluation protocol remain fixed.
five_step_recipe: Measure and stratify the residual.
Tie one residual component to a physical mechanism.
Expose that component to the correction path.
Match capacity and compute controls.
Remove or permute the residual signal and test downstream return.
tactical_cards.differentiation_within_parent: Unlike redesigning the generator, this preserves it and liberates one measurable unexplained residual.
robotics_failure_modes: Residual leaks target labels.
Correction capacity rather than mechanism explains the gain.
Residual is defined after observing results.
tactical_cards.decisive_experiment: Remove the mechanism-aligned residual channel under matched capacity and require performance to return toward the fixed-generator baseline.
tactical_cards.semantic_negative_control: Use a magnitude-matched residual with shuffled time, contact or object correspondence.
tactical_cards.prior_art_search_signature: robotics residual mechanism sim-to-real friction contact dynamics error correction matched capacity
step_by_step_recipe: Measure and stratify the residual.
Tie one residual component to a physical mechanism.
Expose that component to the correction path.
Match capacity and compute controls.
Remove or permute the residual signal and test downstream return.

tactical_cards.name: Cross-modal shared representation
tactical_cards.tactical_move: Align vision, touch, language, proprioception or force into a task-usable state.
tactical_cards.when_to_apply: Use when modalities are complementary but not jointly actionable.
success_conditions: Each modality has a leave-one-out test.
Alignment improves a downstream decision rather than only retrieval similarity.
failure_modes: The common space is a concatenation with no causal use.
tactical_cards.trigger: Complementary modalities exist but cannot jointly affect a downstream decision through a stable interface.
tactical_cards.changed_object: Modality-specific observations are mapped into a shared task-usable state.
tactical_cards.retained_invariant: Downstream policy, training budget, task split and sensor availability remain controlled.
five_step_recipe: Define the distinct information supplied by each modality.
Specify the shared state and alignment constraint.
Expose the shared state to one downstream decision point.
Run leave-one-modality and misalignment controls.
Test held-out sensor noise, delay and missing-modality conditions.
tactical_cards.differentiation_within_parent: Unlike generic fusion, this requires cross-modal alignment to be causally used by the robot decision loop.
robotics_failure_modes: Timestamp or frame mismatch creates false complementarity.
One modality dominates and the shared space is unused.
Training labels leak alignment.
tactical_cards.decisive_experiment: Hold downstream capacity fixed and compare correct alignment with modality permutation; only correct alignment should improve the task decision.
tactical_cards.semantic_negative_control: Time-shift or identity-permute one modality while preserving its marginal statistics and tensor shape.
tactical_cards.prior_art_search_signature: robot multimodal shared representation vision touch force proprioception alignment downstream control
step_by_step_recipe: Define the distinct information supplied by each modality.
Specify the shared state and alignment constraint.
Expose the shared state to one downstream decision point.
Run leave-one-modality and misalignment controls.
Test held-out sensor noise, delay and missing-modality conditions.

tactical_cards.name: Heterogeneous regime decomposition
tactical_cards.tactical_move: Split contact, terrain, object, user or agent regimes and allocate distinct treatment.
tactical_cards.when_to_apply: Use when a single controller or policy averages incompatible regimes.
success_conditions: The partition variable is measurable online or at design time.
A single-policy control fails under the same budget.
failure_modes: The partition is tuned after results or has no operational meaning.
tactical_cards.trigger: One controller or policy averages regimes with incompatible dynamics, observations or objectives.
tactical_cards.changed_object: The predeclared regime partition and allocation rule.
tactical_cards.retained_invariant: Total data, compute, tuning budget, task and denominator remain matched.
five_step_recipe: Demonstrate incompatible regime signatures.
Choose an observable predeclared partition variable.
Allocate distinct treatment under a fixed total budget.
Compare with one pooled model and random partitions.
Test unseen transitions and partition errors.
tactical_cards.differentiation_within_parent: Unlike solver delegation, this first establishes heterogeneous regimes and then allocates treatment by a measurable partition.
robotics_failure_modes: Partition labels leak outcomes.
Per-regime models receive more total capacity.
Transition regions are omitted.
tactical_cards.decisive_experiment: Under the same total budget, replace the meaningful partition with pooled and random partitions and test both regimes plus their transitions.
tactical_cards.semantic_negative_control: Use a frequency-matched random partition unrelated to contact, terrain, object, user or agent regime.
tactical_cards.prior_art_search_signature: robot heterogeneous regime decomposition mixture controller terrain contact user matched budget
step_by_step_recipe: Demonstrate incompatible regime signatures.
Choose an observable predeclared partition variable.
Allocate distinct treatment under a fixed total budget.
Compare with one pooled model and random partitions.
Test unseen transitions and partition errors.

tactical_cards.name: Decompose and delegate to solvers
tactical_cards.tactical_move: Give typed subproblems to specialized planners, learned policies, agents or tools.
tactical_cards.when_to_apply: Use when planning or coordination contains separable subproblems.
success_conditions: Interfaces and failure recovery are explicit.
Coordination cost is included in the end-to-end evaluation.
failure_modes: A pipeline of modules is called a contribution without a unifying interface.
tactical_cards.trigger: A task contains typed subproblems with different solver structure and a monolithic solver fails or scales poorly.
tactical_cards.changed_object: The task is partitioned into explicit solver responsibilities and interfaces.
tactical_cards.retained_invariant: End-to-end task, information access, total compute and recovery budget remain matched.
five_step_recipe: Identify separable subproblems and their ownership.
Specify typed inputs, outputs and failure states.
Assign the smallest competent solver to each subproblem.
Add bounded coordination and recovery behavior.
Compare end-to-end quality, cost and failure against a monolithic baseline.
tactical_cards.differentiation_within_parent: Unlike regime decomposition, this delegates algorithmically distinct subproblems rather than choosing treatments for data regimes.
robotics_failure_modes: Interfaces hide privileged state.
Coordination latency erases solver gains.
One solver failure cascades without recovery.
Budget matching omits orchestration cost.
tactical_cards.decisive_experiment: Disable or replace one delegated solver at a time and verify the predicted typed failure while accounting for full orchestration cost.
tactical_cards.semantic_negative_control: Randomly swap solver assignments between type-compatible interfaces while preserving module count and compute.
tactical_cards.prior_art_search_signature: robot task decomposition specialized solver delegation interface recovery planner policy tool
step_by_step_recipe: Identify separable subproblems and their ownership.
Specify typed inputs, outputs and failure states.
Assign the smallest competent solver to each subproblem.
Add bounded coordination and recovery behavior.
Compare end-to-end quality, cost and failure against a monolithic baseline.

tactical_cards.name: Feasibility-object re-casting
tactical_cards.tactical_move: Replace an open-ended deployment goal with an explicit operating envelope and feasibility object.
tactical_cards.when_to_apply: Use when field performance fails because the target was never bounded.
success_conditions: The envelope is measurable before deployment.
The resulting claim is falsifiable and transferable.
failure_modes: The envelope is selected after seeing the result.
tactical_cards.trigger: A deployment goal is too open-ended to yield a reproducible success or failure statement.
tactical_cards.changed_object: The goal becomes a measurable operating envelope plus a feasibility decision.
tactical_cards.retained_invariant: Robot capability, task meaning and safety limits are not weakened after outcomes are observed.
five_step_recipe: Enumerate the deployment variables and hazards.
Predeclare the measurable operating envelope.
Define feasibility and abort decisions inside that envelope.
Sample boundary and interior conditions.
Report both feasible regions and observed failure regions.
tactical_cards.differentiation_within_parent: Unlike sequential recasting, this changes an unbounded deployment target into a bounded feasibility object rather than temporal phases.
robotics_failure_modes: Envelope excludes known hard cases after the fact.
Safety stops are counted as successes.
Coverage is dense only near nominal operation.
tactical_cards.decisive_experiment: Evaluate predeclared interior and boundary cells and require predicted feasibility transitions without post-hoc envelope edits.
tactical_cards.semantic_negative_control: Use an equal-size envelope chosen from irrelevant variables and show it does not predict success/failure boundaries.
tactical_cards.prior_art_search_signature: robot deployment operating envelope feasibility boundary field robustness safety stop
step_by_step_recipe: Enumerate the deployment variables and hazards.
Predeclare the measurable operating envelope.
Define feasibility and abort decisions inside that envelope.
Sample boundary and interior conditions.
Report both feasible regions and observed failure regions.
